title: Review of Practice to Rank Teachers for Performance
what_it_is: Review of Practice to Rank Teachers for Performance

sections.label: Teacher performance cross-department ranking
sections.summary: A teacher's performance is assessed by their supervisor and cross-ranked against peers by a ranking panel of direct and indirect supervisors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
sentences.text: As performance evaluation involves qualitative judgement by supervisors, the Singapore Civil Service, like many large organisations, practises cross-department ranking.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
sentences.text: A teacher's performance is assessed by his or her own supervisor, and then cross-ranked against his or her peers by a ranking panel comprising direct and indirect supervisors.

sections.label: Principals paid by substantive grades
sections.summary: In recent years, more than 80% of principals are remunerated according to their substantive grades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In recent years, the majority of, and, in fact, more than 80% of our principals are being remunerated according to their substantive grades.

sections.label: 360-degree feedback as development tool
sections.summary: The 360-degree feedback mechanism is used as a development tool to gather all-round feedback, not for appraisal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Rather than for appraisal, the 360-degree feedback mechanism is used as a development tool to gather all-round feedback.

sections.label: MOE performance ranking same grade
sections.summary: MOE follows the Civil Service in conducting performance ranking for officers of the same substantive grade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Currently, MOE follows the Civil Service, which is, to conduct performance ranking for officers of the same substantive grade.

sections.label: Cross-ranking and awards review
sections.summary: Newly appointed principals should be compared with peers in the same substantive grade, and MOE has reviewed awards to avoid unnecessary competition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: When this happens, obviously then, it is not a very good and fair way for us to measure the performance of the newly appointed principal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And this is really why, in this case, using this example, the newly appointed principal should actually be compared with his or her peers in the same substantive grade which is why we are doing such cross rankings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Earlier on, Ms Denise Phua said it also depends on whether the immediate supervisor is more vocal and whether or not the educator is doing certain projects that are more visible.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: And this is why, other than taking the inputs of the direct supervisor, we complement the individual assessment by the direct supervisor with also the views of the ranking panel which will comprise direct and also indirect supervisors who have worked with a broad base of educators, to ensure that we arrive at a fair and just assessment for our educators.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As for the Member's second suggestion about doing away with awards, in the last few years, MOE has reviewed many of these awards and we try to strike a good balance to ensure that it does not inadvertently create unnecessary competition and pressure.
